title: A-flat Major Piano Chord (Ab): Notes, Inversions & PDF
description: Find the A-flat major piano chord: A-flat, C and E-flat. Compare its inversions, keep the spelling clear and print the keyboard reference.
user_task: Locate this exact triad and compare its three bass positions.
questions: Which note is natural in A-flat major?
Does the PDF include finger numbers?

blocks.heading: Notes and keyboard position
blocks.body: A-flat major is A-flat, C and E-flat. Its formula is 1–3–5, with C as the major third above A-flat. The displayed root-position example is A♭4–C5–E♭5. Numbers after note letters identify octaves, not fingers. Use the diagram, note list and bass label together; Play chord sounds the selected notes together, while the note-by-note control sounds them from low to high.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实] rules; [推断] register and original teaching example

blocks.heading: What to notice
blocks.body: Two chord tones use black keys, but the third C is natural. Do not lower C merely because the root name contains a flat. The accidental belongs to its written note unless another notation instruction says otherwise. From A-flat, C is four semitones higher and E-flat is seven. A-flat major is not A major with only its root lowered: moving the entire A–C♯–E shape down a semitone gives A♭–C–E♭.
blocks.evidence_status: [推断] original explanation from preserved note data and cited rules

blocks.heading: Compare three positions
blocks.body: Read each bass note before selecting a position. The root-position example starts with A♭; first inversion starts with C; second inversion starts with E♭. The chord tones stay the same. These are independently chosen reference registers, not an ascending exercise. Switching a position must update the selected note order, diagram, sound and current-print snapshot together. Hand numbers, when available, apply only to the root example.
blocks.evidence_status: [推断] derived inversion explanation; controls are implementation acceptance requirements
